questions.question: Slippery surfaces make it hard to control a motorcycle. Which surface is slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all slippery. Ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: Motorcycle signals are:

options.text: Not very important since motorcycles are small.
Very important to warn other drivers of your plans.
Not needed if no vehicles are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very important to warn other drivers of your plans.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more vulnerable. Always use turn signals when turning or changing lanes, even if no other vehicles are near you.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used on curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: Keep more distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: It is harder to stop than usual.
You want to look at the view.
You want other drivers to cut in front of you.
You want the driver ahead to not know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder to stop than usual.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy. These conditions make stopping harder.

questions.question: Street-legal motorcycles must have all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Street-legal motorcycles must have a headlight, taillight, brake light, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors.

questions.question: When you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Expect it to ride like your own motorcycle.
Trust that the owner checked the brakes.
Give yourself extra space and time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give yourself extra space and time to react.
questions.explanation: Check a borrowed motorcycle before riding it, just like you would your own. Ride cautiously and allow extra stopping distance since the bike is unfamiliar.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: A helmet protects best when it:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: ____ removes alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers can keep you awake but cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Do a quick inspection of your motorcycle before every ride. This takes only a few minutes and helps prevent dangerous problems.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: It protects your eyes and face.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your eyes and face the best. Regular eyeglasses are not enough protection. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still a good idea to wear one.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator be more visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective material. Always use your headlight. Use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a bridge grating?

options.text: Always stay on the far right side of the lane.
Always stay on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave. This is usually not dangerous. Just stay calm and cross at a steady speed. Do not zigzag, as this could make you lose control of your lane.

questions.question: What should a rider do when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Keep more distance between you and other vehicles.
Let air out of the tires for the extra weight.
Do not tell your passenger about road hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. You should stay further away from other vehicles to stay safe.

questions.question: If you wait one hour for each alcoholic drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system. Even after waiting, you may still feel the effects and your riding could be unsafe.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your ability to ride?

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be impaired before reaching the legal limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing your lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
Which position gets you there faster.
Which position lets you pass more vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you. Make sure you have enough space around you in case you need to stop or avoid something.

questions.question: What can reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in so other drivers do not notice you.
Do not use turn signals unless it is nighttime.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Follow the vehicle ahead very closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To avoid accidents, be visible to others. Use your turn signals, brake light, and position yourself well in the lane. Stay far enough away from other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: What type of boots or shoes should a motorcycle rider wear?

options.text: Tall shoes that cover and support the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tall shoes that cover and support the ankle.
questions.explanation: Wear tall, sturdy boots that support your ankles. Keep heels low so they do not catch on anything. Tuck in long laces so they do not get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which item is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves. Sandals do not protect your feet.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are used to show rules. Speed limit signs are white with black text. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Prevent brakes from activating if the roadway is dry.
Warn you when your brake pad needs replacing.

questions.explanation: ABS stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard. When sensors detect a wheel is about to lock, the system releases and reapplies brake pressure. This keeps your motorcycle from skidding.

questions.question: A person with a minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. You cannot legally operate a motorcycle or car if your BAC is at or above this level.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is a good idea to drag your feet.
Your toes should be pointed downward.
You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
You should try to keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for good balance. Do not drag your feet on the ground. Do not point your toes down, as they may hit the road. Keep your feet close to the controls so you can use them quickly.

questions.question: Your primary source for information about your motorcycle should be:
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your motorcycle. It has details about how your motorcycle works and how to maintain it.
